findings.description: If RESTORE_PATHS lists a path and also something under it (e.g. ".agents .agents/skills"), the second pass lists the same symlink entry again, `ln -s --` fails with "File exists", and under bash -e the step dies. The old `cp -R` tolerated this. The shipped lists don't overlap; `ln -sfn --` or a note that entries must not overlap would close it.

The info/exclude append is the one non-obvious line in the new block without a why comment. It keeps the snapshot out of `git status`, so the clean-tree checks stay clean. Without that said, a maintainer could delete it as dead weight.

The `.claude-pr-agents` literal is repeated across the workflow step (5x), SKILL.md, tests and docs. Nothing ties SKILL.md's pointer to the directory the step writes, so a rename in one place would leave reviewers reading a path that no longer exists, with no failing test.

restoreRepo hardcodes RESTORE_PATHS "AGENTS.md .agents", while this repo's workflow runs "AGENTS.md .agents templates". The cross-path behavior is therefore tested on a different list from the one that ships here.

`rm -rf "$path"` follows a symlink the PR commits as a leading component of a multi-component RESTORE_PATHS entry (e.g. `shared/agents` with `shared` committed as a link), deleting outside the checkout. The shipped single-component entries are not exposed, but the RESTORE_PATHS comment invites adding nested directories.

process_issues.description: A `git ls-tree` call needed approval and did not run. The reviewer confirmed the tree layout by listing the restored checkout instead. The claude-code-action source was not readable, so the claim that it empties `.claude-pr/` (restore-config.ts:280) went unverified by context, docs and security.
